name: VA-10
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's 6-point Democratic lean plus a favorable national environment
Prediction markets price Democratic win at 94-95%
First-term incumbent with no serious outside spending against him
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Subramanyam: a D+6 district, incumbency, a favorable environment, and a roughly 11-to-1 fundraising advantage over Dave Beckwith. Markets on both Kalshi and Polymarket price the Democratic win around 94-95%, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: A major national backlash wave or unexpected outside spending against Subramanyam could pull the margin toward single digits.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
First-term Democrat Suhas Subramanyam defends a Northern Virginia seat that leans Democratic by about six points, in what the broader environment favors his party. He has raised over $1.1 million and holds roughly $583,000 on hand, while Republican Dave Beckwith has raised about $107,000 with modest cash reserves. No outside groups are spending against the incumbent, and no independent polls of the race are available.

Prediction markets on Kalshi and Polymarket both price the Democratic win probability in the mid-90s. With no expert raters flagging the race as competitive and no polling suggesting otherwise, the evidence points to a comfortable incumbent win, though the absence of polls leaves some room for uncertainty.
